headline: GOLD $4,390 AND SILVER $65: FOMC BINARY ARRIVES TUESDAY — HERE'S WHAT $4,200 SUPPORT AND $4,500 RESISTANCE MEAN
snippet: Going into Sunday September 13, COMEX gold sits at $4,390 per ounce — up modestly from Friday's $4,348 settlement — while silver trades near $65.19, recovering from Thursday's PPI-driven 4% slide. The Federal Reserve's two-day FOMC meeting convenes Monday September 15, with the rate decision at 2:00 p.m. ET Tuesday September 16 and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET. Markets have priced a hike with roughly 87–90% probability after August's hot core CPI of +0.3% month-over-month. Technicians are focused on two price levels into Tuesday: $4,200, the structural support floor set by central bank buying (244 tonnes Q1 2026 alone) and six consecutive weeks of institutional ETF inflows — a break below this level on a hike-plus-hawkish dot plot would signal a deeper correction phase through October; and $4,500, the next significant resistance level on a hold or dovish 'one-and-done' signal, which JPMorgan has cited as its Q4 2026 gold target. Silver's story is different: the gold-silver ratio at ~67.5 is above the 50-year average of 60, and any FOMC hold or dovish surprise should compress the ratio sharply, with silver potentially recovering $67–$70. For retail investors in junior mining equities, the key variable on Tuesday is not the hike itself — it is Warsh's language about the forward path. A hold or a hike framed as the last move should re-rate GDX and GDXJ from their post-CPI consolidation.

headline: SONORA COPPER GOES VERTICAL: ALGO GRANDE HITS 30m AT 1.5% CUEQ — 100m ABOVE PRIOR HOLES, HIGH-GRADE SKARN GROWING
snippet: Algo Grande Copper Corp. (CVE: ALGR) released Phase II assay results on September 11 from its Cerro Grande skarn discovery at the Adelita Project in Sonora, Mexico. Hole AG-CG-PH2-002 returned 30.23 metres grading 1.5% copper-equivalent (CuEq) from 146.70 metres depth, including a 3.55-metre high-grade core at 9.4% CuEq and a 1.20-metre interval grading 15.8% CuEq. The critical geometric discovery: the mineralized interval lies 100 metres vertically above the mineralization established in Phase I drilling, confirming that the high-grade, multi-horizon skarn system is shallower than previously modelled. Mineralogy is garnet-rich skarn with abundant chalcocite — a copper sulphide with direct metallurgical pathways. The Phase II program, executed by Major Drilling Group International, is simultaneously testing the maiden Cerro Potrero South and Las Trancas programs on the broader Adelita system. For investors watching copper explorers in Tier-2 Mexico jurisdictions: a skarn system that is demonstrably growing upward in grade and adding new mineralized horizons 100 metres above the known envelope, at a time when LME copper recently hit $14,875 per tonne before the September pullback, represents a compelling resource growth thesis. Sonora is an established mining state with infrastructure, and skarn deposits at this grade-width combination historically support bulk-mining feasibility studies.

headline: FOMC WEEK: EMPIRE STATE MONDAY, ADP WEDNESDAY, RATE DECISION TUESDAY — THE FIVE DATA EVENTS THAT WILL MOVE METALS
snippet: The week of September 14–18, 2026 is the most data-dense since January's CPI shock, with five major events that directly affect gold, silver, and mining equities. Monday September 14: New York Empire State Manufacturing Index — a weak print could ease rate-hike odds slightly. Tuesday September 15: ADP Employment report — any softness in private payrolls shifts the FOMC calculus. The FOMC two-day meeting begins Monday, with the rate decision at 2:00 p.m. ET Tuesday September 16. Wednesday September 16: Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET — the dot plot and forward guidance language carry more weight than the binary rate outcome. Thursday September 17: August Industrial Production — measures the real economy's demand for base metals. Friday September 18: Baker Hughes rig count and options expiry on major gold/silver contracts. The Bloomberg Commodity Index is near its highest level in over a decade, and several strategists warn that continued commodity strength complicates the Fed's inflation fight well past September. For junior mining investors, the key framework is not the Tuesday decision but the Wednesday dot plot: if the September Economic Projections show rate cuts beginning before mid-2027, the metals complex would have its clearest dovish signal of the cycle.

headline: WALL STREET FLIPS BULLISH GOLD AHEAD OF FED — ANALYSTS SAY HIKE IS ALREADY PRICED, EYES NOW ON THE DOT PLOT
snippet: A September 11 Kitco survey of Wall Street analysts shows a decisive flip to bullish positioning on gold ahead of the FOMC meeting — despite nearly universal expectation of a 25-basis-point hike. The analytic consensus: at 87–90% probability, the hike is already priced into gold's current $4,348–$4,390 range, meaning the rate decision itself carries limited marginal information. What Wall Street is now positioning for is Warsh's press conference and the dot plot. If the dot plot signals this is the last hike of the cycle, or projects rate cuts beginning in early 2027, gold would have room to rally 3–5% immediately on the unwinding of defensive hedges. If the dot plot shows additional hikes ahead, the correction could deepen toward $4,200. Main Street retail sentiment, however, clings to a slim bullish majority but remains divided — a pattern that historically precedes sharp moves in either direction as event risk resolves. For junior mining equity investors, the Wall Street flip is significant: institutional capital is not waiting for the hike to resolve before positioning — it has already moved. The risk is now asymmetric to the upside if Tuesday's language is dovish, because the bearish trades have largely been placed ahead of the decision.

headline: $54B COPPER DEAL CLEARS SOUTH KOREA — BEIJING IS THE LAST GATE BEFORE ANGLO-TECK BECOMES WORLD'S #2 COPPER MINER
snippet: The proposed $54 billion merger between Anglo American and Teck Resources has cleared every regulatory hurdle except one: China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) antitrust review. South Korea granted approval in early September 2026 — the final Western jurisdiction — and Canada's Investment Canada Act approval was granted December 15, 2025. CEO Duncan Wanblad has confirmed Anglo American is in active engagement with Chinese regulators and targets deal completion between September 2026 and March 2027. The combined entity, to be headquartered in Vancouver, would create 'Anglo Teck' — a copper-focused mining group ranking among the world's top two copper producers by volume, with exposure to copper, iron ore, aluminium, and zinc across five continents. For junior copper investors, the strategic significance is in what this merger signals about where the tier-one miners believe copper prices are going: a $54 billion commitment to copper concentration at $14,000+/t LME copper is a 10-year forward bet on the structural deficit. If China approves, Anglo Teck's acquisition appetite for quality TSX-V and ASX copper developers is likely to re-emerge post-integration — they will need to replenish the resource pipeline they are buying rather than building.

headline: IRAN WAR'S HIDDEN COPPER CASUALTY: HORMUZ SULFUR BLOCK LEAVES CHILE 125,000 TONNES/MONTH SHORT OF ACID
snippet: An analysis from MINING.COM identifies the sulfuric acid shortage — not the LME tariff debate — as the underreported structural threat to copper supply in 2026. Roughly 20% of global copper mine production uses hydrometallurgical (SX-EW) leaching, a wet-process method that requires vast quantities of sulfuric acid. The Iran conflict has closed the Strait of Hormuz to Gulf sulfur shipments — the primary feedstock for producing sulfuric acid — while China, facing a domestic deficit, suspended all sulfuric acid exports to protect its fertilizer industry. Russia extended its own export ban through June 2026. The result: Chile, the world's largest copper producer, faces a monthly shortage of approximately 125,000 tonnes of sulfuric acid. Spot acid prices have doubled, with spot-market procurement exposed producers facing direct margin compression. Wet-process copper accounts for nearly 1.7 million tonnes per year globally; if 10–15% of that output is disrupted, the supply impact rivals the entire annual production of a mid-tier copper producer. Integrated smelter operations — those that produce acid as a byproduct of concentrate processing — are emerging as structural winners, while pure SX-EW leach operators face both input cost inflation and potential output curtailments. For investors screening copper developers and producers, this creates a differentiation argument: underground sulphide projects feeding concentrators are now more competitive than open-pit oxide heap-leach operations dependent on spot acid procurement.

headline: ARIZONA OXIDE GOLD-SILVER SCALES: AZTEC TOMBSTONE HITS 83.8m AT 1.31 g/t AUEQ, STRIKE NOW PAST 1,250 METRES
source_name: Streetwise Reports / Aztec Minerals Corp. (CVE: AZT)
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (CVE: AZT) announced September 2 that RC drilling at the Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona has extended the Contention mineralized system to over 1,250 metres of continuously drilled strike length, with Streetwise Reports providing expanded analysis on September 9. The headline result from hole TR26-41 returned 83.8 metres grading 0.90 g/t gold and 22.61 g/t silver (1.31 g/t gold-equivalent), including a 7.6-metre high-grade core at 6.97 g/t gold and 75.42 g/t silver (8.34 g/t AuEq). The mineralization is oxide — heap-leach processable without sulphide refractory treatment — a critical economic advantage at the current development stage. The September 2 results represent a 255-metre step-out beyond the prior program boundary. Ninety-three RC holes have been completed in the 2025–2026 program, with nine holes (TR26-45 to TR26-53) pending assay. A maiden resource estimate is targeted for Q4 2026. For investors evaluating heap-leach oxide gold-silver systems in US Tier-1 jurisdictions: 1,250+ metres of continuous drilled strike in a single mineralized system, with multiple intercepts exceeding 80 metres width and high-grade sub-intervals reaching 8+ g/t AuEq, constitutes the scale threshold that attracts resource estimate modelling and initiates M&A screening from mid-tier producers. Tombstone's historic namesake district adds jurisdictional familiarity for institutional investors.

headline: CORE LITHIUM HITS SEPTEMBER QUARTER TARGET: FIRST FINNISS SPODUMENE CONCENTRATE PRODUCED, DECEMBER SHIPMENT NEXT
snippet: Core Lithium (ASX: CXO) has produced its first spodumene concentrate from the recommissioned processing plant at the Finniss Lithium Operation in the Northern Territory — achieving the milestone in line with its September Quarter 2026 target, within six months of announcing the Final Investment Decision to restart Finniss in March 2026. Mining resumed at the Grants open pit on May 20, 2026; commissioning of the processing plant followed in August, and concentrate production was confirmed during September 2026. The first shipment of newly produced spodumene concentrate is targeted during the December Quarter 2026, with production and shipments continuing into 2027 and ramp-up to nameplate capacity of approximately 1.2 million tonnes per year expected by mid-2028. The Finniss restart is underpinned by AUD 320 million in available funding and a $274 million underground contract awarded to Develop Global for the BP33 underground mine — a 10-year underground mine life that brings Finniss's total project life to approximately 20 years. For lithium investors, the Finniss first concentrate delivery is a de-risking milestone: the plant works, the logistics chain is operational, and a Chinese spodumene buyer will receive the first shipment in Q4 — confirming that Australian hard-rock spodumene supply from a restarted operation is flowing as modelled.

headline: SOUTH32 TOPS UP AMERICAN EAGLE GOLD NAK STAKE — C$50M TREASURY ADVANCES BC COPPER-GOLD PORPHYRY TO NEXT CATALYST
snippet: South32 Limited exercised its contractual 'top-up right' on September 8, 2026, purchasing 660,000 shares of American Eagle Gold Corp. (CSE: AEA) at C$1.09 per share for gross proceeds of C$719,400 — maintaining its 19.9% strategic equity interest in the company as provided under an investor rights agreement signed November 26, 2024. The top-up follows American Eagle's broader equity raises throughout 2025–2026 and confirms South32's ongoing conviction in the Nakinilerak (NAK) Copper-Gold Porphyry Project in British Columbia's Skeena Country. American Eagle now holds more than C$50 million in its treasury dedicated to advancing NAK. For junior mining investors, South32's maintenance of a 19.9% ownership interest — the maximum allowed before triggering a formal takeover bid obligation under Canadian securities law — is a well-understood strategic signal: a $10 billion market-cap major is holding the exact threshold position that positions it as the preferred acquirer without committing to a bid price. Every dollar South32 spends to maintain this position is an affirmation of NAK's strategic value. The project targets a large copper-gold porphyry system in a jurisdiction with established infrastructure and a track record of major mine development.

headline: BRIXTON LANGIS TAILINGS PROGRAM: ALL 85 HOLES RETURN SILVER — 61.7 g/t AVERAGE ACROSS 120m AT COBALT CAMP HISTORIC SITE
snippet: Brixton Metals Corporation (TSX-V: BBB) reported September 8 that its 2026 maiden tailings characterization program at the Langis Silver Project in the historic Cobalt silver mining camp of Ontario returned silver mineralization in all 85 sonic drill holes — an exceptionally consistent result for a historical tailings study. The program intersected an average of 119.5 metres of tailings per hole on a length-weighted basis, with an average grade of 61.7 g/t silver. Individual highs reached 810 g/t silver. The Langis Project is part of the historic Cobalt District, which produced more than 600 million ounces of silver during its operating life from the early 1900s. Brixton has simultaneously been generating extraordinary hard-rock drill results in 2026: the company previously reported 2.3 metres of 1,811 g/t silver within 27.7 metres at 166.45 g/t silver (June 2026), 5,015 g/t silver over 20 metres in a new brownfields discovery area (July 2026), and the all-time highlight of 6,199 g/t silver over 1 metre including 0.50 metres at 12,386 g/t silver (September 2). With silver at $65/oz and a sixth consecutive annual deficit of 46.3 million ounces confirmed by the Silver Institute, Brixton's 2026 tailings characterization provides dual optionality: the hard-rock resource continues to expand at extraordinary grades while the tailings resource offers a heap-leach or bioleach surface-processing pathway that does not require underground development.

headline: 762 MILLION OUNCES AND COUNTING: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT ANNUAL DEFICIT WIDENS TO 46.3M OZ IN 2026
snippet: The Silver Institute, citing research by British firm Metals Focus, projects the 2026 global silver market will record its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit — widening 15% to 46.3 million troy ounces from the 2025 shortfall of 40.3 million ounces. The cumulative undersupply since 2021 has now reached approximately 762 million ounces — more than 85% of one full year of global mine production. The deficit is structural rather than cyclical: primary silver mine output has stagnated as lead-zinc-copper mines (which produce most of the world's silver as a byproduct) face declining grades and reserve depletion, while demand has accelerated across solar panels, semiconductor packaging, and EV charging infrastructure — all of which require silver in the manufacturing process that cannot be substituted at current price levels. Separately, China reclassified silver from an ordinary commodity to a strategic material on January 1, 2026, imposing new import and export controls that have affected trading patterns without yet showing a definitive supply impact. For retail investors holding silver miners or physical silver: 762 million ounces of cumulative undersupply represents a structural drawdown of above-ground stocks that has historically preceded sharp price re-ratings when investor demand re-enters the market. With silver at $65/oz and the gold-silver ratio near 67.5 — above its 50-year average of 60 — the deficit data argues that silver is structurally undervalued relative to the physical supply picture.

headline: BOSS ENERGY HONEYMOON FY2026: PRODUCTION UP 61% TO 1.4M LBS — BUT THE WELLFIELD RESET IS THE REAL STORY FOR BULLS
source_name: The Motley Fool Australia / Boss Energy Ltd. (ASX: BOE)
snippet: Boss Energy (ASX: BOE) reported August 27 that its Honeymoon uranium project in South Australia produced 1.4 million pounds of U3O8 in FY2026 — a 61% year-on-year increase — with a C1 cash cost of A$39 per pound and all-in sustaining cost (AISC) of A$61 per pound. The company also achieved a profit turnaround for the full year. However, the result that matters most to long-term uranium investors is not the production number but the wellfield geometry reset: Boss initiated a comprehensive redesign of the Honeymoon in-situ recovery wellfield in December 2025, moving from tight ~40-metre spacing to a wider 75–150 metre spacing that is expected to significantly improve uranium recovery rates, flow consistency, and cost efficiency. A new feasibility study incorporating the redesigned wellfield was targeted for release at the end of August 2026. With uranium spot near $90/lb and term contracts at 18-year highs of $96.50/lb, the economic backdrop makes the Honeymoon wellfield reset more valuable than the production headline: at $90+ uranium, even an operation with 40% better recovery economics at the same nameplate capacity represents a substantially different NPV. Boss's pipeline — which also includes advancing Gould's Dam and Jasons toward production — positions it as one of very few in-situ recovery uranium operators with active development outside Kazakhstan.
